news.title: ONU aprova proposta do Brasil de turismo amigável para muçulmanos
news.summary: A ONU Turismo aprovou a proposta brasileira que prevê serviços turísticos que acolham as necessidades culturais e religiosas dos viajantes muçulmanos. A iniciativa foi aprovada por aclamação durante sessão nesta terça-feira (24) da ONU Turismo, em Abu Dhabi, e teve o endosso de Indonésia, Irã e Nigéria, além de marcar o fim da presidência do Brasil no Conselho Executivo da organização entre 2025 e 2026. Notícias relacionadas: Incubadora vai apoiar empreendimentos de afroturismo no país. Brasil supera meta de turismo internacional para 2026. A proposta surgiu a partir de experiências em São Paulo e Foz do Iguaçu (PR) , traz parâmetros para a promoção do turismo Muslim Friendly e tem como base o Guia Nacional de Turismo Amigável aos Muçulmanos. Com a aprovação pela organização internacional, torna-se referência global. A proposta prevê a criação de um termo comum para diferenciar a hospitalidade acolhedora (Muslim Friendly) da certificação halal formal (que atesta que um produto foi feito seguindo a Lei Islâmica), criação de critérios para acolhimento e alimentação, estabelecimento de locais de oração, privacidade nas acomodações e serviços específicos durante o Ramadã (período sagrado para os muçulmanos, marcado pelo jejum durante o dia e renovação espiritual). Ainda está previsto padronizar infraestrutura religiosa e cultural, implantar plataformas digitais multilíngues e capacitar profissionais do setor de turismo. A adesão dos países às orientações é voluntária. Cada um poderá fazer as adaptações para as demandas locais. O Guia Nacional de Turismo Amigável aos Muçulmanos foi elaborado pelo Ministério do Turismo em parceria com a Federação das Associações Muçulmanas do Brasil (FAMBRAS), a Câmara de Comércio Árabe-Brasileira, a Embratur e a International Halal Academy.

news.title: 'Nothing will ever be the same' for Jensen Huang and Nvidia after his return

news.title: Ucrania denuncia el nombramiento para la dirección del OIEA de un funcionario ruso bajo sanciones

news.title: AFCON: Ten months on, court to rule on 2025 winner
news.summary: Ten months after the Africa Cup of Nations final was chaotically played on the field between Morocco and Senegal, the title will be awarded Tuesday by sports’ highest court. The Court of Arbitration for Sport set the target Monday to publish the verdict of its panel of three judges on Senegal’s appeal to regain the title the team won on the field in Morocco in January and then lost in a legal case in March.

news.summary: What does it feel like to blast off in a rocket and what happens to a spaceship in a meteor shower? These are some of the questions sent in by children to French astronaut Thomas Pesquet as he joined France 24 to share his experience on board the International Space Station.

news.title: ICE raids add to jitters ahead of Thanksgiving travel rush
news.summary: Travellers in the US are heading into a particularly stressful holiday travel period this week. Recent network outages for US airlines and the Federal Aviation Administration have raised concerns about flight delays and cancellations ahead of Thanksgiving on Thursday. This, plus ICE agents ramping up arrests at airports, has made many travellers anxious.

news.title: How cautious investors are struggling to avoid the AI bubble

news.title: Thousands evacuated from UK concert after release of 'unknown substance'
news.summary: British police said they evacuated 12,000 people from ​a concert venue in Manchester, northern England, after the release of an "unknown substance" required some in the crowd to be treated and one person to be taken to hospital. Police ​declared ‌a major incident late on Sunday after staff at the ⁠Co-op Live arena alerted them at 10 p.m. (2200 GMT) that people in the crowd had fallen ill during ‌a performance by US rapper Don Toliver.

news.title: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang

news.title: Was Jensen Huang too big to fire? Why Nvidia, Trump brought him back
news.summary: Nvidia chief's 'mistakes' had consequences far beyond Silicon Valley. He is back nonetheless, in less than two weeks.

news.title: Israeli air strikes in Gaza kill 7 as doctors warn of meningitis outbreak
news.summary: Gaza health officials say meningitis cases rose to 272 in October, more than eight times the typical monthly rate.

news.title: Spain set to head to polls in snap election that could boost far right
news.summary: Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez seeks to thwart grim polls as polarised Spain holds an election on Sunday that could propel the opposition conservative Popular Party (PP) and the far right to power. The outcome will be closely watched across Europe as it opens a cycle of elections over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the European Union.

news.title: Is Russia preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite?
news.summary: German media reports, citing unnamed German military and BND spy agency sources, have claimed that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite in the coming weeks, giving it the capability to destroy other satellites. In response, NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space. France 24’s correspondent in Berlin Nick Holdsworth has the details.

news.title: Republicans, Democrats unite in anger over Trump's Nvidia intervention
news.summary: Members of Congress responded with swift, bipartisan fury Monday over the Nvidia board's surprise decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang at the behest of US President Donald Trump, opening a new phase of questions about the chipmaking giant and potential national security lapses. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look.

news.title: Nvidia's position as cornerstone of AI trade confirmed by market reaction to Huang's return
news.summary: Tech shares in Asia and Europe rebounded on Tuesday, following in the footsteps of Nvidia's shares closing on Wall Street 31 percent higher on Monday. The return of CEO Jensen Huang, 11 days after his resignation over an extramarital affair with an alleged Chinese spy, has reassured investors in the AI trade. In this edition, we look at Nvidia's central role in this trade, and Huang's central role at Nvidia. Also, French President Emmanuel Macron proposes to enshrine fiscal rules in the constitution.

news.title: Accused of ‘emptying the coffers’, Macron mulls spending caps for future French governments
news.summary: Right-wing candidates vying to succeed French President Emmanuel Macron have welcomed his suggestion of a “golden rule” to cap government spending and keep deficits in check, even as they mock the profligacy of his decade in power. Critics of the proposal denounce a budgetary straitjacket imposed on future governments and a distraction from the president’s growing impotence at home.
